title: Latency splinter sync notes - 2026-10-19
content:
Meeting: micro-splinter latency-sync (standup-style)
Date: 2026-10-19 10:00 PT
Attendees: Elliot, Aisha, Marta, Jun, Daniel (joined 10:12)
Duration: 35m
Purpose: align on isolated low-volume p99 spikes that 'splinter' into two populations during mixed workloads; capture test runs and next steps.

1) Quick recap (Elliot)
- Started seeing recurring ~200-300ms p99 spikes on a small fraction (~0.7%) of requests during the 10–12k QPS shadow runs last week. Average tail persists when mixed seqs are present.
- Termed this pattern "splinter" because latency distribution shows two distinct clusters rather than a smooth tail.
- Related ticket: JIRA-RTR-1423.

2) Observed signal summary (Aisha)
- Baseline (control): multi-tenant shadow run w/ batching heuristic v3, qps ~11.5k, avg latency 38ms, p95 72ms, p99 baseline 182ms.
- Splinter runs: p99 spikes jump to ~420ms on a tiny slice; CPU/GPU utilization unchanged, no host flapping.
- Correlation: spikes correlate with requests that trigger a cold KVCACHE miss on longer sequences (>1024) that then follow with a burst of small requests that beat on the same worker.
- Metric evidence: increased websocket queue depth in trace ids, and a bursty kernel scheduling event visible in node perf counters.

3) Hypotheses brainstormed
- H1: KV cache eviction race — concurrent evict + rehydrate causes synchronous stall to service thread.
- H2: Batching heuristic path mispredict for mixed sequence lengths leads to temporary micro-starvation of inference worker (one worker temporarily processes very large sequence then small ones queue behind).
- H3: CUDA kernel warmup/first-call overhead for a particular fused-kernel variant for sequence length around 1k triggers the larger latency cluster when that kernel is chosen dynamically.
- H4: Sidecar (tracing/logging) sampling introduces blocking when trace payloads attach to the request under specific headers.

4) Tests run during sync (what we executed)
- Run A (Jun): Replayed captured trace window (2026-10-15 02:14) with KV caching disabled. Result: splinter frequency dropped from 0.7% -> 0.05%. p99 median for affected window fell from 410ms -> 190ms.
- Run B (Marta): Shadow run with batching heuristic forced to conservative mode (batch cap per-worker = 4). Result: spike frequency unchanged but spike magnitude decreased slightly (~410ms -> 360ms).
- Run C (Daniel, later): Forcing fused-kernel fallback to older kernel (PR attempt: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987). Result: no splinter observed in short window (10k requests), but end-to-end throughput dropped 6%.
- Run D (Aisha): Disabled sidecar trace enrichment for that route. Result: no measurable change.

5) Preliminary conclusions
- KV-cache behavior strongly implicated (Run A changed frequency substantially). Kernel variant likely amplifies severity when it occurs (Run C reduced occurrence but impacted throughput). Batching heuristic may modulate magnitude but not root cause.

6) Action items (owners & timelines)
- Aisha: Create a focused benchmark that isolates the KV-cache lifecycle: eviction pattern + rehydrate hotspots. Deliver script + run results by 2026-10-22. (JIRA: RTR-1423-1)
- Jun: Add additional instrumentation around KV-cache eviction boundaries (timestamps, thread ids, blocking flags). Short patch to add lightweight counters; PR by 2026-10-21. (RTR-1423-2)
- Marta: Run a longer-duration experiment forcing kernel fallback at 1M requests to measure throughput impact and potential mitigation (increase run window, collect perf counters). Results due 2026-10-25. (RTR-1423-3)
- Daniel: Prototype optimistic rehydrate path (async rehydrate with in-flight placeholder token) to avoid synchronous stall; spike a prototype branch and run unit microbench by 2026-10-26. (RTR-1423-4)
- Elliot: Coordinate canary rollout plan for kernel fallback / KV mitigations if a clear mitigation emerges. Draft runbook by 2026-10-28.

7) Short-term mitigations to try (non-blocking)
- Increase default batch cap per-worker temporarily to smooth scheduling (low-risk config change) — Marta to test in staging.
- Reduce KVCACHE max-evict-chunk-size to avoid large synchronous evict loops — Jun to run local microbench.
- Conservative kernel selection for the hot route as a canary (via route override) to observe production impact slowly.

8) Notes on data / artifacts
- Trace samples: collected sample ids: trace-20261015-0214-a1..a6 (stored in s3://redwood-traces/splinter/2026-10-15/).
- Benchmark scripts live: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-scripts/tree/splinter-kv-tests (branch: splinter-kv-work).
- Perf counters snapshot: node-3-perf-2026-10-15-0214.json attached to JIRA-RTR-1423.

9) Risks & escalation
- If optimistic rehydrate increases memory tail or introduces correctness issues, we must gate behind integration tests. Daniel to add mem/regress tests.
- Kernel fallback may reduce throughput and increase cost — coordinate with cost/infra before wide rollout.

10) Open questions (to resolve next sync)
- Are there specific model families more likely to trigger evictions? (Elliot to query model-catalog for seq-length histograms).
- Do multi-tenant hotspots happen from single customer bursts or cross-tenant mixing? (Prod logs team to correlate tenant ids where allowed).
- Can we add rate-limited background rehydrate to amortize cost? (R&D feasibility check).

11) Next sync
- Tentative: 2026-10-22 09:30 PT. Focus: Aisha test results, Jun instrumentation PR, initial prototype runs from Daniel.

Informal notes / friction items (scratchpad)
- Quick Slack thread: #serving-runtime; pinned message with earliest trace. Some folks accidentally ran heavy profiling on prod proxy during early reproductions -> avoid.
- Need a short one-pager for SOC/compliance describing why trace payload reduction is safe for a canary (Marta to draft).

End.
